claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 9 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 9 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children. 

**What is the age of the child or children you're claiming for?**

To help you properly, I need to know:
1. How many children do you have that you're wanting to claim for?
2. What are their ages (or date of birth)?
3. What are their names?

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 9 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I just want to make sure I'm eligible before I apply.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Let me guide you through the eligibility assessment for Alex.

Since Alex is 9 years old, he falls into the "under 16" category, which means he automatically qualifies as a qualifying child. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news so far! Now I need to ask:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is 9 years old, I expect the answer is yes (not in full-time work), but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 9! He's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected. Since Alex is 9 and in primary school, he's definitely not working. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

Again, given his age (9), I'd expect the answer to be yes, but let me confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a kid!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to ask about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Given his age (9 years old and in primary school), I'd expect the answer to be no, but I need to confirm for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 9 and still in primary school. He's nowhere near starting an apprenticeship!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Since Alex is not in an apprenticeship, let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. You mentioned that Alex lives with you here in the UK. Let me ask:

**Which of the following best describes your situation?**

1. **Normally resident in the UK** - You normally live in the UK
2. **Settled status** - You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. **Pre-settled status** - You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (and if so, I'd need to know more about your circumstances)
4. **Crown servant abroad** - You're living abroad as a Crown servant

Based on what you've told me so far (you and Alex live here in the UK), I'd expect you fall into category 1 (normally resident in the UK). Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I normally live in the UK. We're based here permanently.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That confirms you meet the residency requirements. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. You've already mentioned he lives with you, so this should be straightforward.

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This can be through:

1. **Living with the child** - You live with Alex (which you've already confirmed ✓)
2. **Contributing to upkeep** - You pay towards his food, clothes, housing, etc.
3. **Maintenance payments** - You make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement

Since you've confirmed Alex lives with you permanently, you clearly meet the responsibility requirement. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely - Alex lives with me full-time and I provide for all his needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You clearly meet the responsibility requirement. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask about any other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or could anyone else claim for him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent also potentially claiming or planning to claim for him?
- Is any other relative or guardian claiming for him?

Or is it just you claiming for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's just me - nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex currently:**

1. **In hospital** - Admitted to hospital?
2. **In care** - In local authority care?
3. **Fostered** - With foster carers?
4. **Living normally** - Living with you at home?

Based on what you've told me, I'd expect Alex is living with you at home. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex lives at home with me. He's not in hospital, care, or fostered.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost there. Just one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for all of Alex's care yourself, or is the local council helping to pay for his accommodation or upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - I'm covering all his costs myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! That's the final check complete. Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! 🎉

## **You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

You meet all the eligibility requirements:

✅ Alex is under 16 years old  
✅ He's not working full-time  
✅ He's not receiving certain benefits in his own right  
✅ He's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship  
✅ You normally live in the UK  
✅ You're responsible for Alex (he lives with you full-time)  
✅ No one else is claiming for him  
✅ He's living at home with you  
✅ The council isn't paying towards his accommodation or maintenance  

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate**
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, there may be a charge to reclaim some of the benefit
5. **Payments** will be made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can start your application here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Congratulations, and best of luck with your application!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's brilliant, thank you so much! Really helpful to know I'm eligible. I'll get the application sorted out. Thanks for walking me through everything!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm so glad I could help and that you have clarity on your eligibility. You've got all the information you need to move forward with your application.

Just to recap:
- You're **eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**
- Make sure you have his birth certificate and proof of identity ready when you apply
- Remember to check the High Income Child Benefit Charge if it applies to your circumstances
- Head to https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim to start your application

If you have any other questions about Child Benefit or need further assistance in the future, feel free to reach out. Good luck with everything, and best wishes for you and Alex! 😊
